record.paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
record.context_brief: Good for equality versus good ultrafilters
record.original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter. If D is good for equality, must C(D) be empty? Equivalently, must D be good, where good means |I|^+-good: every monotonic function from finite subsets of |I| into D has a multiplicative refinement? Equivalently, if D admits internal maps between small sets in the sense captured by good-for-equality, must D also admit internal order-preserving maps between small increasing sequences?

evidence.quote: Say that D is good if it is |I|+-good.
General Problem 3.5. Let D be a regular ultrafilter. If D is good for equality, is C(D) = ∅?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let I be an infinite index set and let D be a regular ultrafilter on I (regular: there exists a family {X_i : i ∈ I} ⊆ D such that every index of I lies in only finitely many X_i). 

For a cardinal λ, D is called λ-good if every monotonic function f: [λ]^{<ω} → D (i.e., u ⊆ v implies f(u) ⊇ f(v)) has a multiplicative refinement, that is, a function g: [λ]^{<ω} → D with g(u) ⊆ f(u) for all u and g(u ∪ v) = g(u) ∩ g(v) for all finite u, v. Say D is good if D is |I|^+-good.

Say D is good for equality if for every set X with |X| ≤ |I| and every function h: I → X, there exists a "distribution" producing internal representatives realizing equality types: more precisely, for every such h there is a refinement assigning to each pair (i, j) the truth value of h(i) = h(j) in a way that is multiplicative on D, capturing the existence of internal maps between small sets up to D-equality.

Let C(D) denote the set of cuts (a, b) in the linear order (ω, <)^I/D of cofinalities (κ_1, κ_2) with κ_1, κ_2 regular uncountable cardinals ≤ |I| that are not realized in this ultrapower (equivalently, the "symmetric cut spectrum" of D as customarily defined for regular ultrafilters).

Question: If D is good for equality, must C(D) = ∅? Equivalently, must every regular ultrafilter that is good for equality be good (i.e., |I|^+-good)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a general open problem in the literature on ultrafilter saturation and Keisler's order. Recent works by Malliaris and Shelah (including ultrafilter-construction papers through 2025) continue to discuss good-for-equality as a distinct property whose relation to goodness and to realization of symmetric cuts remains an active line of research, with no resolution found in the searched sources.

status_evidence.title: On ultrafilter construction (Malliaris)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses properties of ultrafilters including flexibility, goodness, goodness for equality, and realization of symmetric cuts as distinct properties under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Good-for-equality is treated as a separate property whose relation to goodness is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Cofinality spectrum theorems in model theory, set theory and general topology
status_evidence.snippet: Any good ultrafilter is good for equality; saturating SOP2 implies good for equality; if C(s,ts) = ∅ then there is a minimum non-simple class in Keisler's order.
status_evidence.claim: The implication good ⇒ good-for-equality is known; the converse for regular D, equivalent to C(D)=∅, is posed as an open question.
